abstract: A radioimmunoassay for a plancental glycoprotein, beta1SP1, capable of detecting 2 microgram/l of the glycoprotein in serum was used to measure concentrations of beta1,SP1 in patients with choriocarcinoma, teratoma, colonic cancer, breast cancer, and ovarian cancer. 12 out of 94 (13%) healthy men and health non-pregnant women had detectable serum-beta1SP1 concentrations. Concentrations up to 50 000 microgram/l were found in the sera of patients with hydatidiform mole, invasive mole, choriocarcinoma, and malignant teratoma. beta1-glycoprotein concentrations were generally much lower than corresponding concentrations of chorionic gonadotrophin which is the most reliable marker for trophoblastic tumours. In a few cases, however, beta1-glycoprotein measurements may be useful in the detection of minimal residual tumour. The slightly raised values found in some patients with carcinoma of the colon, breast, or ovary seem unlikely to be useful for diagnostic purposes of for monitoring the course of these cancers.
abstract_ja: ヒト胎盤性糖タンパクβ1SP1を検出する放射免疫測定法（血清中2 µg/Lまで検出可能）を用い、絨毛癌、奇形腫、大腸癌、乳癌、卵巣癌の患者におけるβ1SP1濃度を測定した。健常男性および非妊娠女性94名中12名（13%）で血清β1SP1が検出可能であった。胞状奇胎、侵入奇胎、絨毛癌、悪性奇形腫の患者血清では最大50,000 µg/Lの濃度が認められた。β1糖タンパク濃度は、栄養膜腫瘍の最も信頼できるマーカーとされるヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピンの対応濃度よりも概して著しく低かった。しかしながら、少数例では、β1糖タンパク測定が微小残存腫瘍の検出に有用である可能性がある。大腸癌、乳癌、卵巣癌の患者でみられた軽度上昇は、これらの癌の診断目的や経過観察には有用でないと思われる。
